page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr9i.xlarge belongs to the High Clock Speed instance family, built on the KVM hypervisor and designed for applications demanding both high single-core compute performance and a high ratio of system memory. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor running at a base clock speed of 3.4 GHz, the server provisions 4 dedicated vCPUs alongside 32.0 GB of system memory, resulting in an allocation of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring persistence to be managed via remote cloud disk options. Networking capabilities are configured with a 4 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and it does not feature hardware GPU acceleration or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The 1:8 core-to-memory ratio provides significant memory capacity relative to compute allocations, prioritizing in-memory data processing without necessitating larger vCPU footprints.

This hardware profile suits workloads requiring low compute latency combined with generous memory footprints, such as in-memory caching tiers, relational database engines, high-frequency transaction processing, and enterprise application servers.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr9i.xlarge is a high-clock-speed, memory-dense virtual machine within the High Clock Speed family, powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor operating at 3.4 GHz, complemented by 32.0 GB of memory to yield an 8.0 GB RAM per vCPU profile. The instance provides 4 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and includes no local disk storage, relying on external network-attached volumes for persistent data. Lacking dedicated GPU hardware accelerators, its architecture focuses directly on high-frequency CPU execution paired with an expanded memory pool. This structural balance makes the server suitable for in-memory databases, caching layers, relational database hosting, and memory-bound transactional enterprise workloads.
